doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Playing on 'Bull Durham' and loving records; Snooky's many sessions
summary: He earns residuals from a trumpet solo in 'Bull Durham', prefers playing on records, and recalls Snooky Young's multiple sessions a day.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Do you still get an occasional check in the mail?
Can you tell me something that you might hear that you’d go, “oh I was on that.”

Oh I was on a movie called “Bull Durham.” Baseball movie. And it was just me. And it was just in one scene. And I must have played that thing 40 times. I remember the guy’s name was Michael Convertino. He was the composer. And it was just trumpet. That’s all it was. Maybe with synthesizer or something. It was just a kind of a dramatic scene in the locker room. And I’ve made so much money off that thing. And I didn’t play that many. But I just was lucky to get called for it. I mean I’m on some movies and stuff. But that’s not my pride really. I love playing on records. I’ve played on probably a hundred records or more, which sounds maybe like a lot but when you talk about Snooky Young or Joe Wilder, Snooky played on a thousand records.
That used to be a hobby of mine with LPs, sort of like, “oh there he is again.”
And you’d see these guys move from one thing to another.

Oh yeah. Especially in New York. Snooky said he’d have like four sessions a day sometimes. You know? He wouldn’t even go home. He’d just get a hotel room. Because the next day he’d have a bunch. He looked at me one day and said, “it was great.”
